annotations.text: Parameter-tree read-back, no simulation: the April rise in the rate PolicyEngine-UK holds. April 2026 rates are legislated amounts entered in the tree, so those comparisons check the entry, not a model.

PolicyEngine-UK uprates CPI-linked working-age rates by gov.benefit_uprating_cpi, which follows OBR's calendar-year CPI forecast lagged one year (2.30% for 2026 in the March 2026 EFO), not the September rate the law uses. Tracked in PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk#2533; PR #2557 moves the index to September CPI and enters 3.5% for September 2026.
annotations.basis: policyengine-uk 2.147.2 parameters/gov/benefit_uprating_cpi.yaml (uprating: gov.economic_assumptions.indices.obr.lagged_cpi); OBR EFO March 2026 Table 1.7, calendar year 2026; https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk/pull/2557

annotations.text: policyengine-uk 2.147.2 has no September 2026 outturn: statutory_uprating_inputs.cpi_september is null for 2026, so the model uses its own forecast. That forecast sets the income tax thresholds and the Universal Credit Act 2025 s. 4 floor for the protected health element.

PolicyEngine-UK sets the UC standard allowance as CPI-only uprating from 2025-26 plus the Universal Credit Act 2025 uplift (2.3%, 3.1%, 4.0% and 4.8% for 2026-27 to 2029-30, not compounded), so its April 2027 to 2029 rises move with its CPI forecast.
